sources.title: Zipf's Law and Cache Hit Ratios: Why Your Caching Math Fails When ...
sources.snippet: If you assume a strict Zipfian distribution, the relationship between cache size and hit rate is non-linear. The first few gigabytes of cache yield massive rewards, but you quickly hit a point of diminishing returns where adding more memory barely moves the needle.

sources.title: A New Upper Bound on Cache Hit Probability for Non-anticipative Caching Policies
sources.snippet: Caching systems have long been crucial for improving the performance of a wide variety of network and web based online applications. In such systems, end-to-end application performance heavily depends on the fraction of objects transferred from the cache, also known as the cache hit probability. Many caching policies have been proposed and implemented to improve the hit probability.
